headline: DDT won a Nobel Prize. Then bird eggs broke.

portrait.alt: Photograph of Paul Müller smiling, in a dark suit and tie, in front of a tree trunk
portrait.credit: Paul Müller, 1951. Willy Pragher, Landesarchiv Baden-Württemberg. CC BY 4.0.

slides.label: The bright idea
slides.title: Kill the bugs that kill us
slides.text: Lice spread typhus, mosquitoes spread malaria, and the best insect killer had to be sprayed weekly. **Paul Müller went looking for a better one.**

slides.label: It worked
slides.title: A powder against typhus
slides.text: In 1939 he found DDT killed insects on contact. In Naples in 1944, **DDT was among the powders dusted on 50,000 people a day.**

slides.label: The backfire
slides.title: Thin shells
slides.statLabel: bald eagle nesting pairs in the lower 48 in 1963, by a federal count
slides.text: DDT lingered and built up in fatty tissue. **Some birds of prey laid shells 19 percent or more thinner.**

slides.label: Could anyone have seen it coming?
slides.title: Partly
slides.text: In 1946 US wildlife biologists published a study of DDT's effects on fish and wildlife. **The thinning shells were measured only after Müller died.**

slides.label: The long cleanup
slides.title: Banned, with one exception
slides.text: The US canceled DDT in 1972, and a treaty now bans it except against malaria mosquitoes. **Bald eagles recovered and came off the federal list in 2007.**

slides.label: The ledger
slides.title: Worth it?
gains: Over 50,000 people a day dusted against typhus lice in Naples, 1944, DDT among the powders
Malaria spraying once or twice a year instead of every week
Italy declared malaria-free in 1970, after spraying began in 1947
costs: 417 bald eagle nesting pairs left in the lower 48 states in 1963
Eggshells 19 percent or more thinner in three declining US birds of prey
Residues still in the environment decades after the US ban
slides.text: DDT saved people from two of the oldest killers there are. **The bill went to birds, rivers and the food chain.**

slides.label: Pattern
slides.title: Too stable to go away
slides.text: On a wall DDT lasted six months or more, where the old spray lasted a week. **Outdoors, that same staying power let it build up.**

slides.label: Lesson
slides.title: What we take from it
slides.text: The trait that made DDT work was the one that made it a problem. **Ask where your fix goes when its job is done.**
